2. The present appeal arises against order dated 21.11.2023 passed by the High Court of Jharkhand in Cr.M.P. No. 3712 of 2022 whereby the Court dismissed the appellants petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 19731 seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceedings,
including the FIR, chargesheet and order of the S.D.J.M., Ramgarh taking cognizance, in connection with S.T. No. 216 of 2022 arising out of FIR No. 1 CrPC 146 of 2018.
3. The facts leading up to the present appeal arise from the marriage between the appellant husband and respondent no.2wife, which was solemnized on 08.12.2010 according to Hindu customs.
Admittedly, the parties stayed together only for a brief period of fifteen days and thereafter respondent no.2 returned to her parental house.
Since respondent no.2 refused to return to the matrimonial home, appellant initiated divorce proceedings under section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 19552.

The parties subsequently consented to mutually dissolve their marriage and thus a decree of divorce by mutual consent was passed by the Family Court on 22.05.2014 upon a joint application signed and submitted by both the parties.

4. Subsequently, the respondent no.2 filed a miscellaneous case seeking declaration of the 2 HMA order of the Family Court a nullity on the grounds that her signatures on the consent form were false Ranjeet Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13128250/
1 and fabricated.

sentences.text:
This miscellaneous application was later dismissed by the Family Court vide order dated 10.08.2022 with the observations that the date and necessary details regarding fraud on the part of non-applicant have not been mentioned in miscellaneous application which is necessary and also that the respondent no.2 herein had admitted her signature on the joint application for dissolution of marriage.
5.
She also filed a complaint before the State Women Commission alleging fraud and forgery by the appellant.

This complaint, registered as Case No. 611 of 2014, was dismissed vide order dated 06.01.2016 for no evidence being brought on record to suggest that an appeal had been filed against the divorce decree.

Respondent no.2 got another complaint registered against the appellant, before the C.J.M. Nawada, under section 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 192 of the Indian Penal Code, 18603 alleging that the appellant had fabricated the signature of respondent no.2 on the joint application for divorce by mutual consent.

6. After four years of passing of the divorce decree, FIR No. 146 of 2018 dated 20.10.2018 was registered at the instance of respondent no.2 against the appellant and his family members for offences under sections 498(A), 341, 342, 323, 325, 307, 364, 376(B), 136, and 34 of the IPC.
It was alleged in the FIR that two months after the marriage, the appellant and his family members started demanding dowry and the appellant would torture and assault her repeatedly for the same.
She was consequently abandoned from her matrimonial house and then threatened several times over phone calls with the appellant.
She went back to her matrimonial house upon a compromise entered between the parties but the accused persons continued to harass and torture her.
They assaulted her brutally several times and 3 IPC confined her in a room without any food for several days.
The appellant allegedly took her signature on a blank paper by coercing her, which she later discovered was used to obtain a decree of mutual divorce.

That despite the parties having been divorced, the victim had been confined in her matrimonial house for days and was also sexually assaulted by the appellant under the pretext of a lawfully subsisting marriage.
She had never appeared before the Family Court and was never aware of the divorce proceedings, but still her signatures were present and the decree of divorce was obtained fraudulently.
Thus, she was subjected to hurt, wrongful confinement, wrongful restraint, and sexual assault by the appellant and his family members.
It is the proceedings arising from this FIR which are before us for consideration.

7. The Investigating Officer filed a charge-sheet on 23.10.2020 against the appellant under sections 498-A, 341, 342, 323, 325, 307, 364, 376B, IPC and sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
No evidence was found against the other six co-accused persons (family members of the appellant) and thus they were not named in the charge-sheet.
The S.D.J.M., Ramgarh vide order dated 31.10.2020 took cognizance in the case on the basis of the charge-sheet upon finding a prima-facie case being made out against the appellant.

8. Appellant approached the High Court in Cr.M.P. No. 3712 of 2022 under Section 482 of the CrPC seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceedings including the cognizance order passed by the S.D.J.M. in connection with the FIR No. 146 of 2018 on the grounds of prolonged and unexplained delay in filing the FIR, improper investigation, mala fide intentions of the complainant to harass the appellant and his family in order to extort money, and no prima facie evidence of the alleged Ranjeet Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13128250/
2 incidents.

sentences.text: Vide the impugned order, the High Court refused to quash the criminal proceedings upon finding no merit in the prayers except for delay in filing the FIR.

9. Upon hearing the counsels for the parties and perusing the material on record, this Court finds that the delay in filing the FIR, combined with the nature of the allegations, raises serious questions regarding the credibility and motivation of the complaint lodged by respondent no.2.
The delay of more than four years post-divorce without plausible explanation points towards an intent to harass the appellant rather than to pursue justice for genuine grievances.

The respondents actions,
including multiple unsuccessful attempts to challenge the divorce decree on grounds of alleged forgery and fraud, suggest a pattern of vexatious litigation aimed at intimidating the appellant.

10. The Family Court, in its order dated 10.08.2022, dismissed the miscellaneous application challenging the mutual consent divorce on grounds that lacked substantiation, observing that respondent no.2 had herself admitted her signature on the joint application for divorce.

Additionally, the complaint registered with the State Women Commission was dismissed on 06.01.2016 due to a lack of evidence to support the claim that any appeal had been filed against the divorce decree.

Despite these repeated dismissals, respondent no.2 continued to raise allegations,
culminating in the registration of FIR No. 146 of 2018.
11.

It is also noteworthy that the allegations brought forward in the FIR, including accusations of dowry demand, confinement, and sexual assault, were not raised in any of the prior proceedings,
whether before the Family Court, the State Women Commission, or the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Nawada.
These serious allegations have surfaced for the first time in 2018, four years after the divorce was finalized.
The respondents failure to mention such critical claims in prior legal filings and complaints raises substantial doubts about their authenticity.

It is highly improbable that allegations as severe as those involving wrongful confinement, physical abuse, and sexual assault would have been omitted from her earlier applications if they had genuinely occurred.

12. Moreover, the Investigating Officer, after due investigation, did not find sufficient evidence to proceed against the six co-accused (family members of the appellant), further suggesting a lack of corroborative evidence to support the respondents allegations.
This reinforces the appellants contention that the complaint was filed with malicious intent, is totally vexatious and based on concocted facts.
13. The High Court, in its order dated 21.11.2023, failed to consider these material aspects and declined to quash the proceedings.

However, as per established legal principles, this Court holds that when the very basis of a criminal proceeding appears to be malafide or intended to harass the accused, such proceedings must not be allowed to continue.

This Court has consistently held that abuse of process in criminal law must be addressed firmly by exercising inherent powers under Section 482 of the CrPC to prevent misuse of the judicial machinery.

14. In light of the facts and circumstances, including the lack of prima facie evidence, the delayed filing of the FIR, and the absence of any allegations in earlier proceedings, this Court is of the opinion that permitting the prosecution to proceed in this case would amount to an abuse of the Ranjeet Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13128250/
3 judicial process.

15. The appeal is allowed.
All criminal proceedings arising from FIR No. 146 of 2018, including the charge-sheet filed on 23.10.2020 and the order of cognizance passed by the S.D.J.M., Ramgarh, on 31.10.2020 are quashed.
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
